messages:
Alex: thinking out loud — can we add a lightweight telemetry "nudge" in the rollout console that surfaces when automatic fallback kicks in frequently? not a full alert, just a small badge and a sample trace.
Mira: +1. product needs a way to judge if fallback is expected noise vs a regression. what do you mean by 'frequently'?
Alex: something like >1% fallback rate over the last 5m for a route, or >0.5% but sustained 30m. fuzzy thresholds, toggleable per-project.
Sam: important: distinguish degrade-mode fallbacks (intentional) vs error-triggered fallbacks. the UI should show breakdown by reason.
Jordan: agree. also we need audit linkage — clicking the badge should show samples and the audit event id so SRE can trace.
Mira: UX idea: badge colored by severity (:yellow_circle: / :red_circle:) and clicking expands a tiny panel with 3 representative requests + timestamps + why they fell back.
Alex: exactly. keep it compact soconsole doesn't get noisy. plus an option to open the full audit playback.
Sam: implementation note: backend should return a compact payload: counts + top-3 reasons + sample request ids. avoid returning full payloads in the widget for PII reasons.
Jordan: sampled ids must map to the audit-store. we should also include a sampling-rate annotation so people understand "we only sampled 1/100 on this flag".
Mira: copy for the panel: "Fallbacks detected. These are requests routed to fallback model/region due to: error rate, latency, or operator policy." quick actions: "Mute badge", "Open audit", "Create ticket".
Alex: what about operator notifications? we don't want to spam PagerDuty for tiny/expected fallbacks. maybe tiered: badge -> email digest -> PD if >X and sustained.
Jordan: yep. PD only for urgent (e.g., >5% sustained over 10m) and when route is production-level. dev routes should be excluded by default.
Sam: API compatibility: rollout-policy API currently returns a `fallback_stats` blob. we can extend it to include `reason_breakdown: [{reason: "latency", pct: 0.6}, ...]` and `samples: ["audit-123", "audit-456"]`. small change and backward compatible.
Alex: can you sketch an example payload?
Sam: sure — snippet:
```
{
  "route": "chat.completion.v1",
  "fallback_stats": {
    "window_secs": 300,
    "fallback_pct": 1.4,
    "reason_breakdown": [
      {"reason": "kv-cache-miss-latency", "pct": 0.9},
      {"reason": "model-error-502", "pct": 0.3}
    ],
    "samples": ["audit-1714007001", "audit-1714007054"]
  }
}
```
Mira: perfect. product note: surface the human-friendly reason labels, not internal codes. e.g., "High decoder latency" vs "kv-cache-miss-latency".
Jordan: security check: make sure samples in the UI are redacted and link to the audit console (authz enforced). the panel should show only metadata: latency, model id, truncated prompt hash.
Alex: UX edgecase: what if the rollout policy intentionally funnels X% to fallback? badge could show "expected (preset 10%)" and not nudge unless observed > preset+alpha.
Sam: good point. policy has `target_fallback_pct`. UI logic: compute observed - target. if delta < 0.5% ignore.
Mira: auditability: every badge click should emit an event so we can track who inspected and when. useful for post-incident.
Jordan: audit-bot: logging sample
audit-bot: AuditEvent created audit-1714007054 route=chat.completion.v1 fallback=true reason=model-error-502 user=alex
Alex: thanks. next steps: Sam to prototype API change, Mira to mock panel copy/colors, Jordan to confirm PD thresholds and auth flows. I'll sketch a tiny spec for the console micro-interaction.
Mira: timeline? this quarter or next?
Sam: small API change + backend aggregator — 2 sprints. UI mockup can land in 1 sprint.
Jordan: I'll validate PD thresholds this week and get a short ops-runbook blurb.
Alex: sounds good. leaving a TODO: (1) API proto, (2) sample redaction rules, (3) badge color mapping, (4) audit event for badge clicks.
Mira: tagging: @Sam @Jordan please follow up in this thread with PR links. :thumbsup:
Sam: will do.
Jordan: on it.
Alex: thanks everyone — keeping this lightweight will make rollouts less scary for product teams.
